author: Antonialock
body:
* **Rule (ID and label):**
ARBA00005098

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
O76895 (D. melanogaster Arg, FBgn0023535)

* **Description of issue**
ARBA00005098 & RU361159 add UniPathway:UPA00158, which then generates a GO annotation of 'urea cycle' (GO:0000050).
But insects don't have a urea cycle (the GO term recently had a taxon constraint added to address this).
title: ARBA2GO issue: ARBA00005098

author: Antonialock
body:
I annotated the mosquito entry and we are adding a taxon constraint to insects to block urea cycle 
based on ref https://resjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/imb.12989

author: deustp01
body: For birds also, there are good reasons to believe that the urea cycle does not operate (accumulation of urea inside a hard-shelled egg during gestation should be lethal), so inferred annotations of [avian enzymes](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/annotations?goUsage=descendants&goUsageRelationships=is_a,part_of,occurs_in&goId=GO:0000050&taxonId=9072&taxonUsage=descendants) that are orthologs of authentic urea cycle participants in other taxa are probably wrong. (For odd historical historical reasons there are some relevant Reactome annotations [here](https://reactome.org/PathwayBrowser/#/R-GGA-372568&SEL=R-GGA-187630&PATH=R-GGA-1660598).)

author: Antonialock
body:
Thanks @deustp01 , yes it looks like the view today is that chickens do not have a functioning arginine cycle (e.g. the reference above and a title of a 2023 paper "Effects of arginine replacement with L-citrulline on the arginine/nitric oxide metabolism in chickens: An animal model without urea cycle "

however the sequencing paper (https://www.nature.com/articles/nature03154) says:
"These data, and the presence of all the other enzymes of the mammalian urea cycle in the chicken genome (data not shown), indicate that this cycle is intact in birds but might perform a function distinct from the generation of urea for excretion."

So I thought I'd leave it for now since I'm not sure if there is a definite answer for all birds?
